item.title: District women council elected in Vanimo Green
item.description: Vanimo Green District Council of Women has elected its President and executive to represent women in the District and Province for the next five years. The district becomes the second in West Sepik Province to complete nominations, after Nuku District.
item.content:encoded:
Vanimo Green District Council of Women has elected its President and executive to represent women in the District and Province for the next five years.

The district becomes the second in West Sepik Province to complete nominations, after Nuku District.

The Elected leaders are, President, Susan Nali representing Bewani Wutung Onei LLG Deputy President, Anna Kane from Green River LLG Secretary, Gerhard Gubon for Vanimo Urban LLG and, Treasurer, Merolyne Yapo for Amanab LLG

Provincial Director for Community Development, Florence Agen, officially opened the nominations and urged the women leaders to be wise and bold in decision making.

"Your work is not only about growing SMEs. Women in this province and country face many issues, starting from Gender Based Violence at home and in workplaces, and even suppressed rights when it comes to voting. You are not just representatives.

“You must use this role and voice these concerns on behalf of all the women you represent in this district, province and country as a whole," said Ms Agen

Agen also called for training to be conducted in each LLG and ward to build the confidence and skills of women leaders.

District Senior Court Magistrate Sasa Ikung administered the oath of office. He told the new leaders that by signing the oath they officially hold office under law and must perform their duties accordingly.

Newly elected President Susan Nali spoke to NBC News after the event.

"I thank God and all my fellow women leaders for entrusting me with this important role. I will do my best with my executive to represent our women well" said Ms Nali

Ms Nali said their first meeting is scheduled for today, Monday 7th September, where LLG and ward women leaders will meet to discuss plans, highlight issues and other areas of concern at the district level.

The District and Provincial Councils of Women are established under the National Council of Women Act 2013.

The Act gives the mandate for women leaders to represent women in government decision making and policy, and provides an avenue for women to voice their concerns as citizens of Papua New Guinea.

item.content:encoded:
Despite the kidnapping for ransom incident at Haiyafuli Village in Bedamuni LLG near Mougulu Station in the Middle fly District of Western Province, students in Grades eight 8, 10 and 12 at Mougulu Secondary School are currently sitting for their mock examinations this week.

School administration confirms there are about 145 students sitting for their mock exams including both day and boarding students.

The Grades 7, 9 and 11 students were sent home for school holidays last week Friday.

With the ongoing security concern at Haiyafuli village on the Western/Hela/SHP border, school officials say the situation at Mougulu remains calm.

Three police officers from Kiunga Police Station have been assigned to Mougulu station to provide support and maintain law and order in the district.

"We are not panicking, but we are taking caution and staying alert," a school source said.

School authorities say exams are continuing as scheduled, with staff and students taking necessary precautions.

item.title: Second communications tower planned for Waria
item.description: A second communications tower is planned for the remote Waria area in Morobe, under a partnership between the Wau Waria District Development Authority and PNG DataCo Limited. The 30-metre carrier-neutral tower will be built at Kamare village, about one kilometre from the Northern Highway.
item.content:encoded:
A second communications tower is planned for the remote Waria area in Morobe, under a partnership between the Wau Waria District Development Authority and PNG DataCo Limited.

The 30-metre carrier-neutral tower will be built at Kamare village, about one kilometre from the Northern Highway.

It will provide mobile and internet coverage to communities in Gataipa, Sim, Gerepo, Wisi and Kasangare, including Kasangare Primary School.

Procurement and shipment of materials are expected to take two months.

Construction is planned to begin in November and finish by February 2027.

The project follows the completion of the first carrier-neutral tower at Kembaka village, which is now in service.

Wau Waria Open MP and DDA chairman Marsh Narewec said the Kamare tower would be available for different mobile network operators.

He said only Vodafone had so far co-located at the Kembaka tower.

“Kembaka was built as a neutral tower, available to all operators.

“We call on Telikom and Digicel to also co-locate at Kembaka and at Kamare.” Narewec said.

Narewec said tower sharing could help reduce costs for operators and eventually lower internet prices for consumers.

The next stage of the Kamare project will include technical surveys and studies before construction begins.

item.title: Police operations underway in Western Province following kidnap and murder case
item.description: Two teenage girls were reportedly kidnapped by armed criminals in Western Province, with one murdered and the other still being held at gunpoint. In a statement, Police Commissioner confirmed a specialist operation underway to rescue the surviving girl, and bring those responsible to justice.
item.content:encoded:
Two teenage girls were reportedly kidnapped by armed criminals in Western Province, with one murdered and the other still being held at gunpoint.

In a statement, Police Commissioner confirmed a specialist operation underway to rescue the surviving girl, and bring those responsible to justice.

Police are conducting a coordinated operation at Haiyafuli Village in Mogulu, Western Province, following reports that two teenage girls were kidnapped and taken hostage by armed criminals.

Police Commissioner David Manning says one of the girls was murdered by her captors, with her remains recovered by Police.

The second girl is believed to be held at another location at gunpoint, as specialist tactical Police continue efforts to locate and rescue her.

One suspected offender has already been shot and killed during the Police response.

Commissioner Manning says Police will use every lawful and necessary means to rescue the surviving girl alive, and has called on the remaining suspects to release her unharmed and surrender.

“This is an ongoing operation in which Police are pursuing dangerous criminals who killed one young woman and continue to hold another girl at gunpoint,” Commissioner Manning confirmed.

“These are desperate individuals who have rejected the basic standards of their own communities and placed themselves outside decent society," he said.

He is also urging communities to support Police by remaining vigilant and refusing to provide shelter or assistance to those responsible.

“Our main priority is the safety and recovery of the young girl they have taken, and Police will use every lawful and necessary means to bring her out alive.

Commissioner Manning says further information will be released as the operation continues.

item.title: PM in Kaintiba
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape arrived in remote Kaintiba Station this morning after 24 hours on the road as part of his Connect PNG maiden drive-through. The Prime Minister received a warm traditional welcome from local leaders and communities gathered at the station.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape arrived in remote Kaintiba Station this morning after 24 hours on the road as part of his Connect PNG maiden drive-through.

The Prime Minister received a warm traditional welcome from local leaders and communities gathered at the station.

While addressing the people at the station, Marape said the national road project will bring essential services closer to rural Papua New Guineans.

He told the people that better roads mean faster access to health, education and business services.

He described the walk-by-talk trip as a symbol of his Government’s commitment to Connect PNG as a life-changing national project.

The Prime Minister also acknowledged contractors and landowners for their support in delivering the project.

He will officially unveil a Connect PNG commemorative plaque marking infrastructure works in the isolated Gulf region before continuing his trip to Lae.

Several senior ministers including Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso and Finance Minister Thomas Opa are traveling with him.

Yesterday at Epo Junction, the PM and Mr. Opa unveiled a Connect PNG billboard, with the Finance Minister saying the highway will reduce transport costs and open new market opportunities for Gulf.

The delegation is expected to depart for Morobe today as the drive-through continues toward Lae, Goroka and Mt. Hagen.

Marape says the maiden road trip symbolizes the connection of the country’s three major cities from Port Moresby to Lae and to Mt. Hagen.

item.title: PM begins maiden road trip
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has departed Port Moresby at 2:30am this morning. The departure marks the start of the Connect PNG maiden drive-through from Port Moresby to Lae and Mt. Hagen.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has departed Port Moresby at 2:30am this morning.

The departure marks the start of the Connect PNG maiden drive-through from Port Moresby to Lae and Mt. Hagen.

The convoy is under full Police and Protocol escort as it begins the 4-day inspection of the Trans-National Highway.

Works department secretary Gibson Holemba says the trip will assess road works and engage with communities along the corridor.

Senior ministers and project teams are traveling with the Prime Minister for the journey.

The first scheduled stop was at Laloki Billboard where the Prime Minister took the opportunity to capture the moment on camera to symbolize the launch on the Hiritano Highway.

More than 50 vehicles with supporters gathered to witness the historic start of the Connect PNG drive.

The Prime Minister said the program is about connecting all provinces by road and boosting economic access.

The convoy is now traveling the Hiritano Highway towards Gulf Province.

item.title: Giant crocodile killed
item.description: A giant crocodile was shot dead this afternoon at Port Moresby’s Adventure Park after it attacked its handler. Initial reports and videos from the scene revealed the gruesome moment the crocodile mauled the staff member.
item.content:encoded:
A giant crocodile was shot dead this afternoon at Port Moresby’s Adventure Park after it attacked its handler.

Initial reports and videos from the scene revealed the gruesome moment the crocodile mauled the staff member.

Park officials and emergency responders struggled for several hours to free the handler from the animal’s grip. The decision was eventually made to kill the crocodile in order to release the victim safely.

St John Ambulance officers attended the scene and provided immediate medical assistance. The injured handler was transported to the 3 Mile General Hospital for urgent medical treatment.

His condition and the full extent of his injuries have not yet been confirmed by hospital authorities.

Adventure Park management is expected to release a full statement following investigations into the incident.

item.title: FRL to take Sepik development project discussions to districts and LLGs in West Sepik
item.description: Frieda River Limited (FRL) will take its community consultations on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to district centres and communities in West Sepik Province. The company will start the district town hall program in Telefomin on September 14, with meetings expected to follow in Vanimo Green, Aitape, Lumi, Nuku and Yangkok.
item.content:encoded:
Frieda River Limited (FRL) will take its community consultations on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to district centres and communities in West Sepik Province.

The company will start the district town hall program in Telefomin on September 14, with meetings expected to follow in Vanimo Green, Aitape, Lumi, Nuku and Yangkok.

The engagements are expected to give communities an opportunity to question the company about the project, express concerns and hear updates directly from its representatives.

Local-level government representatives, community leaders, civil society organisations and members of the public are expected to participate.

FRL Country Manager, Dr. Joel Hamago says taking the discussions into the districts is important because not everyone has access to social media or other platforms where information about the project is being discussed.

He says the company wants to hear from people who may otherwise have limited opportunities to participate in discussions about the project's future.

Dr. Hamago says the meetings will allow communities to seek clarification on issues including project planning, environmental and social management, community development priorities and future consultation.

He says the company expects the face-to-face discussions to help communities better understand the proposed development while allowing FRL to hear directly from people who could be affected by the project.

The town hall engagements are scheduled to run from September through to early November.

The program will cover as many local-level government areas as possible as the company continues its engagement with communities across West Sepik.

The Sepik development project has generated public discussion in the province, making direct community engagement an important part of the ongoing consultation process.

item.title: Madang schools recognised by Education department
item.description: Six primary schools in Madang's Sumkar District were finally recognised by the Education Department this week after they were issued their respective registration codes by the department.
